name: goose

attributes.attribute: taboo food used in divination by Britons

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The goose is a symbolic bird in Celtic myth. People saw the fierce barnyard goose as an image of the warrior divinities, and stone geese lined the temples of Gaul, while Brittany cast bronzes of war goddesses wearing goose-head helmets. So strong was the link that the Britons treated the goose as taboo food, eating it only at rituals and using it in divination.

okr.objective: Present the goose as the Celtic emblem of war and taboo.
key_results: The barnyard goose symbolized warrior divinities.
Stone geese guarded the temples of Gaul.
Brittany made bronzes of goose-head goddesses.
Britons ate goose only on ritual days.
